`ConceptService.saveDrug` is called from four places in the REST module, all in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`. Each is a resource `save` or `purge` override, so a change in `saveDrug` would reach the `/ws/rest/v1` drug, drugingredient and drugreferencemap endpoints on write or delete.

1. **`DrugResource1_8.save`** (lines 66-69): the main `/drug` write path. It passes the posted `Drug` straight to `Context.getConceptService().saveDrug(delegate)`.
2. **`DrugIngredientResource1_11.save`** (lines 169-185): adds the ingredient to its drug if missing, then calls `saveDrug(newIngredient.getDrug())`.
3. **`DrugIngredientResource1_11.purge`** (lines 158-164): removes the ingredient from its drug and calls `saveDrug(drug)` to persist the removal.
4. **`DrugReferenceMapResource1_10.save`** (lines 44-49): adds the reference map to its drug, then calls `saveDrug(delegate.getDrug())`.

The core-side callers of `saveDrug` are the service interface, `ConceptServiceImpl`, and the DAO. The REST module does not call the DAO directly. I did not check the test classes in the REST module (e.g. `DrugController1_10Test`, which calls `saveDrug` at lines 133 and 144), since they are not production code.
